title: EU rules on recycled plastic used in food packaging: updates and clarifications
summary: EU updates rules on recycled plastic production and traceability of food packaging from 18 November 2026
update:
The European Commission has updated its rules on recycled plastic food materials and articles, including packaging, placed on the European Union (EU) market. (For example, “food materials” includes plastic wrap, and “food articles” includes plastic kitchenware.)

These changes cover recycling processes, marketing and use of plastic, and also apply to non-EU exporters of prepacked food products using recycled plastics sold in the EU. In particular, the new Regulation:

Reduces the administrative burden for food operators – operators who use recycled plastic to pack food but do not change the plastic composition are not required to provide a declaration of compliance to retailers or distributors. They can give relevant information on the recycled plastic content through labelling or documentation. Improves traceability by clarifying the information that must be provided by each operator in the supply chain. The Regulation introduces two new compliance documents (in addition to existing Declarations A for plastic recyclers and B for plastic converters): Declaration C, an additional declaration issued by converters and other operators using recycled plastic when they do not change the plastic composition and have either received, or had to issue, Declaration A or B. Declaration P for operators producing plastic inputs for recycled plastic. Simplifies information requirements by removing the need to include batch numbers down the supply chain where the composition of the plastic has not been changed. Initiates the creation of an electronic registration system that will allow recycled plastic operators and competent authorities to manage the status of decontamination installations. Clarifies the rules on the use of plastic offcuts and scrap . Introduces new technical specifications for pre-processed plastic input to improve the quality and consistency of recycled plastic.
impacted_products: Materials intended to come into contact with food
what_changing:
The EU rules on food contact materials containing plastic originating from waste (Regulation 2022/1616 ) cover recycling technologies and processes, manufacturing, marketing, and use of plastic. These rules also apply to non-EU exporters of prepacked food products using recycled plastics that are sold in the EU. For more information, see Plastic food contact materials: basic rules .

Regulation 2026/2376 introduces some changes to these rules, as follows. (Article numbers given below relate to Regulation 2022/1616 , which is amended by the new Regulation.)
why: The proposals aim to improve clarity, ensure better documentation and traceability of recycled plastic content, and simplify controls for businesses and authorities, in response to some needs that were identified during the first years of application of Regulation 2022/1616 .
timeline:
The new rules apply from 18 November 2026 .

For traceability of recycled plastic, the following dates apply:

products already compliant with Regulation 2022/1616 and accompanied by Declaration A or B may continue to be placed on the EU market until 18 February 2027 products that will require the new Declaration C or P may be placed on the EU market without those declarations until 18 May 2027.

Any recycled plastic materials and articles made from products placed on the market during these transition periods may continue to be sold until stocks are exhausted.
background:
Regulation 2022/1616 sets rules for the entire plastic recycling process to be used in food contact materials. Materials and articles intended to come into contact with foods (including packaging) that are made from recycled plastic, and used for products sold in the EU, must comply with these rules. The rules cover the decontamination of recycled plastic, the development and operation of plastic recycling processes, and how these recycled food contact materials are used. They also apply to installations, facilities, and companies based outside the EU. For more information see Plastic food contact materials: basic rules .

Currently, non-EU countries must appoint a national contact point that will contribute to ensuring compliance with the EU rules. These are listed at: Contact points for the competent authorities outside the EU . The European Commission does not provide guidance regarding the designation of competent authorities; each country must establish its own rules and procedures for auditing and controlling recycled plastic recovering installations and facilities. Questions can be emailed to SANTE-FCM-RECYCLING-REGISTER@ec.europa.eu .
title_fr: Règles de l'UE relatives aux plastiques recyclés utilisés dans les emballages alimentaires : mises à jour et clarifications
summary_fr: L’UE met à jour les règles relatives à la production de plastique recyclé et à la traçabilité des emballages alimentaires à compter du 18 novembre 2026
